name: A Change of Scenery: Nature Images, Delay Discounting and Food Desirability
description:
Faithful replication of Clarke, Higgs, Holley, Jones, Marty & Hardman (2021), "A Change of Scenery: Does Exposure to Images of Nature Affect Delay Discounting and Food Desirability?", Frontiers in Psychology 12:782056 (preregistered, OSF jsmk9). Uses the authors' own six natural and six urban scene images from the article's supplementary material (CC BY 4.0).

What participants do: under a "memory and choices" cover story they are randomly assigned to view six natural or six urban scenes, each for 30 s (no skipping), then rate their mood (PANAS, 20 words), answer three memory questions, and complete, in counterbalanced order, (a) the 5-trial adjusting delay discounting task of Koffarnus & Bickel (2014): £5 now or £10 after a delay that starts at 3 weeks and adjusts with each choice, giving ED50 and the discount rate k; and (b) desirability ratings of eight foods (strawberries, raspberries, cucumber, carrots; chocolate-covered doughnut, chocolate buttons, sweets, crisps) on a 0–100 slider. Then age, gender, ethnicity, education, employment, height, weight, eating-disorder history and a guess about the study's aims.

Analysis as in the paper: t-test of k (nature vs urban), MANOVA on healthy and unhealthy food desirability, mediation of nature → healthy food desirability via k, exploratory MANOVA on PANAS positive and negative affect. The paper found no effect of nature images on delay discounting or food desirability (N = 109).

Differences from the original study: (1) The food photos come from Wikimedia Commons (CC0, public domain and CC BY-SA, credited on the end page) because the original food-pics database images cannot be redistributed. (2) The paper does not publish its three memory questions; the template asks how many pictures were shown and whether any showed people or water. (3) The DEBQ restraint subscale is left out because it is a published, copyrighted instrument; add it under your own licence if you need the restraint moderation analysis. (4) Height and weight are optional, and demographic answer options are our own. (5) A short debriefing is shown at the end.

Source and credit: scene images and design come from the authors' article and OSF project and are used with credit; the template is taken down if the authors object.

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I have read the information above and agree to take part.

elements.name: images
elements.title: Image viewing
elements.description: { condition: 'nature' | 'urban', files, seconds_each: 30 } — random assignment; six images shown one at a time for 30 s each (no skipping), with the instruction to study them carefully for a later memory test (cover story).

elements.name: panas
elements.title: This scale consists of a number of words that describe different feelings and emotions. Indicate to what extent you feel this way right now, that is, at the present moment.

columns.text: Very slightly or not at all

elements.description: PANAS, 20 words, 1–5. Positive affect = 01 03 04 06 10 11 13 15 17 18; negative affect = 02 05 07 08 09 12 14 16 19 20. Exploratory MANOVA (nature vs urban).

elements.name: mem_count
elements.title: How many pictures did you see?
elements.description: Memory question (cover story and attention check); correct = 6.

elements.name: mem_people
elements.title: Did any of the pictures show people?
elements.description: Memory question; in the original image sets only urban pictures show people.

elements.name: mem_water
elements.title: Did any of the pictures show water (a river, a lake or the sea)?
elements.description: Memory question; four of the six nature pictures show water, no urban picture does.

elements.name: delay_discounting
elements.title: Money choices
elements.description: { order: 'dd_first' | 'food_first', trials: [{ index, delay, choice: 'now' | 'later', rt }], ed50_days, k, log10_k } — 5-trial adjusting delay task (Koffarnus & Bickel 2014): £5 now vs £10 after a delay; first delay 3 weeks (index 16 of 31), then ±8, ±4, ±2, ±1 indexes (later choice → longer delay). ED50 and k = 1/ED50 from the task's Table 1. Main test: t-test of k (or log k) nature vs urban; mediation of nature → healthy food desirability via k (PROCESS model 4).

elements.name: food
elements.title: How much do you want to eat this food right now?

dimensions.label: How much do you want to eat this food right now?

elements.description: Eight food photos in random order, one per screen, 0–100 visual analogue scale (Not at all … Very much). key = file name: FV_* fruit and vegetables (healthy), ED_* energy-dense foods. Healthy and unhealthy desirability = mean of each four; MANOVA nature vs urban. The delay task and this task come in counterbalanced order.

config.description: Faithful replication of Clarke, Higgs, Holley, Jones, Marty & Hardman (2021), Frontiers in Psychology 12:782056, with the authors' twelve scene images from the article's supplementary material (CC BY 4.0). Participants are randomly assigned to view six natural or six urban scenes for 30 s each, then rate their mood (PANAS), answer three memory questions, make five money choices (£5 now vs £10 later) and rate how much they want to eat eight foods, then give demographics.
